questions: Is the goal to sort the permutation into strictly increasing order (1,2,...,N) or can the target order be specified differently (e.g., decreasing)?
When swapping P_i and P_{i+1}, does the cost i refer to the index before swapping, after swapping, or the smaller/larger of the two values?
Are we allowed to perform swaps in any order, and is the cost additive per swap as given, or are there discounts/penalties for sequences?
Does 'minimum total cost' require considering only sequences that end with a sorted permutation, or must we also ensure intermediate states don't affect cost?
If multiple swaps involve the same index i at different times, do we always pay i each time, even if the elements at positions i and i+1 change?
Is the operation allowed only on adjacent indices, and does 'adjacent' refer to original positions or current positions after previous swaps?
Should the output be an integer, and are there constraints on the cost magnitude (e.g., fits in 64-bit)?
Can we choose i arbitrarily each time, including repeating the same i, and does the cost i depend on the current permutation state?
